To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT for review — Brian’s Monday Embakasi pay briefing, 30 November

DRAFT — Achieng to review before use. For Brian’s preparation on Sunday; not a notice to circulate to the casuals.

Brian,

Thank you for taking this on. After six years working together, I know you won’t need a speech from me about handling people. What you do need is a straight account of what happened, what is actually approved and a plan for the gap between the 6am start, the trucks leaving at 9 and the payment expected by 11.

The starting point is simple: this is our mess, not theirs. They worked, they were due their money on Friday and we failed them. Please don’t go in defending the company or asking them to be grateful for getting what they are owed.

WHAT HAPPENED TO FRIDAY’S PAY

The bank rejected the entire payment file on Friday at 1:52pm. It contained 212 payments. A beneficiary-reference field was too long for the bank’s new template following its 25 November platform upgrade. No payments in that file were processed.

The rejection alert went to the old Finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm, after the bank cut-off. So this was not a case of payments being sent successfully and taking time to appear. Our file failed validation, and we did not pick that up in time to correct it on Friday.

That is enough detail for the explanation at the depot. Own the failure as management; don’t turn the apology into an account of who in Finance missed which email.

WHEN THE MONEY IS EXPECTED

Njeri has approved switching the payments to M-Pesa. Kevin’s current realistic expectation is Monday by 11am. That is the expectation we have, not a guaranteed arrival time and definitely not a promise of payment before loading.

Also approved:
- KES 500 for lunch and fare for every casual on the affected list.
- That KES 500 is to be paid in the same M-Pesa batch as their outstanding pay.
- The company bears the M-Pesa charges. They are not to be deducted from anyone’s pay.

Peninah has confirmed 198 phone numbers. Fourteen people could not be reached, mainly new loaders from the Athi River intake. She will be at Embakasi from 7:30am with the printout to check those numbers face to face, and her laptop for anyone wanting a printed payslip.

We cannot give those 14 an unconditional 11am assurance before their details are checked and Kevin confirms they can be included. Equally, don’t tell them they have lost their pay or the KES 500 because we couldn’t reach them. Get the details corrected and obtain a specific payment update for them.

BEFORE MONDAY’S SHIFT

You are arriving at 5:30. Please find Joseph first and establish what has changed overnight, who is there and whether anyone is already refusing to load. Agree who will keep the loading area safe and who will keep the drivers updated while you speak to the men.

Before the group briefing, speak to Ouma privately, ideally with Joseph available but without making it look like he has been summoned for discipline. He is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four children and rent to find. Start by listening, not by telling him what the trucks need.

Something along these lines:

“Ouma, I wanted to speak to you before we talk to everyone. Your pay should have come on Friday. It didn’t, and that is our failure. I understand people have rent and families depending on it. Tell me what you and the others are most worried about, then I’ll explain exactly what is arranged and what I still cannot guarantee.”

Don’t ask him to carry management’s apology for us or make him responsible for everyone else’s response. Ask whether he and the others will hear you out together.

I am awake from 4:30am. WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes, especially the payment expectation, the mood at the depot or an actual refusal to load. My flight is at 7:05; please don’t assume I will be available immediately after that. We need an agreed HR contact for the period I am in transit, so you are not left handling a stoppage as Operations alone.

WHAT TO SAY TO THE GROUP

Keep it short, then take questions. You can use this in your own words:

“Morning, everyone. I owe you an apology on behalf of management. You worked and your Friday pay did not arrive. You did nothing wrong.

“The bank rejected our payment file because it did not meet the updated file requirements. We did not catch the rejection before the cut-off. No payments from that file went through.

“We have approval to pay through M-Pesa instead. Finance’s current expectation is Monday by 11am. I am not going to promise an earlier time, or tell you it has landed before we have confirmation.

“Each person on the affected list will also receive KES 500 for lunch and fare in the same payment batch. The company is paying the M-Pesa charges; they will not come out of your pay.

“Peninah will be here from 7:30 with the list. There are 14 numbers she could not verify. If yours is one of them, please check it with her privately. She can also help with payslips.

“I know an explanation does not pay rent. I’m asking you to load the Kisumu trucks while we follow the payments through. They need to leave by 9am. I need to be clear that the payment expectation is later than that, so I cannot offer payment before departure as a condition I know we can meet.”

WHAT YOU CAN AND CANNOT PROMISE

You can state the approved payment route, the KES 500, company-paid charges, Peninah’s 7:30 attendance and the current 11am expectation with its qualifications. You can promise to give honest updates, hear concerns and follow up missing payments.

Do not promise “by breakfast”, “before the trucks leave”, “by lunch” or any other substitute deadline. Remember Mombasa in 2024: the supervisor said “by lunch”, the money arrived at 4pm and half the shift sat down. We are not doing that again.

Do not say the money is already sent without Kevin’s confirmation. Do not promise separate cash, an advance, extra compensation or another arrangement that has not been approved. The KES 500 is in the same batch, not cash available at the gate.

No threats about contracts, future shifts or dismissal. No suggestion that asking about unpaid wages makes someone disloyal.

IF OUMA’S GROUP WILL NOT LOAD

The procedure says stoppages are handled by Operations and HR together. It also says no one is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. Follow that even if the conversation gets heated.

1. Establish what is actually happening. Is the whole group refusing, a smaller group, or are people still discussing it? Ask what they are seeking and record their words factually. Don’t label everyone a troublemaker.

2. Bring HR into the response immediately through me or the agreed cover. Joseph can support you, but a supervisor’s presence is not a substitute for HR. Keep the discussion calm and away from moving vehicles and loading equipment.

3. Explain the timing honestly again: the trucks must leave at 9; payment is expected by 11. Ask whether they will resume loading on that basis. Do not claim we can close that gap with an earlier payment unless Kevin has actually confirmed a revised arrangement.

4. If they still refuse, don’t turn it into a public contest with Ouma. Keep dialogue open, document the refusal and the steps taken, and agree the next action jointly with HR.

5. In parallel, manage the transport risk. Work backwards from 9am to identify the latest safe loading start. If departure is becoming doubtful, escalate to Njeri and the transport team early so they can contact the mill about the offloading slot and consider authorised alternatives. Do not wait until 9 to disclose a delay, and do not rush unsafe loading to recover lost time.

PAYMENT FOLLOW-THROUGH

Agree a definite next update time with Kevin before you brief the group. If there is no new information at that time, say so rather than disappearing.

From 7:30, have Peninah deal privately with number corrections and individual pay queries. Don’t read phone numbers or pay details out to the group.

Get confirmation from Kevin of which payments succeeded and which failed or remain pending. A batch being submitted is not proof that everybody has received money. If 11am passes with payments outstanding, acknowledge that the expectation has been missed, get the reason and give the next confirmed update time—not another guessed payment deadline.

The normal grievance route remains supervisor first, then HR within 48 hours. Make sure Joseph records concerns and passes them on promptly. That route must not become an excuse to make people wait another two days for an answer about this pay.

Above all, stay straight with them. We cannot undo Friday on Monday morning. We can apologise properly, avoid another promise we cannot keep, and make sure nobody is left chasing their own wages alone.
